subject: Hospitality
title: The Convention Bureau Model
description: One-minute skill: The Convention Bureau Model.

hook.text: Convention and Visitor Bureaus (CVBs) are city-funded organizations that recruit events to their destinations.

buildup.text: CVBs provide free services to event planners: venue sourcing, hotel block negotiations, site visits, and marketing support.

discovery.text: Las Vegas's CVB spends $250+ million annually on marketing. The return: 40+ million visitors generating $45+ billion in impact.

twist.text: CVBs are funded by hotel taxes—a surcharge guests pay per night. Visitors literally fund the marketing that attracts more.

climax.text: Cities compete fiercely for major events. Hosting the Super Bowl or a medical conference can inject hundreds of millions.

punchline.text: Cities compete to host your event. CVBs turn gatherings into billion-dollar engines.

quiz.question: How are Convention and Visitor Bureaus typically funded?
options: Hotel taxes—a surcharge paid by guests per night
